package_info.package_versions: all published versions (since at least Dec 4, 2023)
package_info.why_malicious: These packages abuse the npm registry by storing and distributing large, non-software media files (pirated movies, video clips, and time-synced user comments) instead of legitimate software artifacts. This violates the platform's terms of service, pollutes the software supply chain, and can be used to circumvent censorship or distribute pirated content.

execution_context.file_location: package root directory (multiple .ts video files, JSON files)

malicious_snippets.code_snippet: [binary .ts video files and JSON files containing time-synced comments]
malicious_snippets.code_behavior: At package publish-time, the package includes large video files (.ts) and JSON files with time-synced comments, enabling the distribution of pirated movies and associated metadata through the npm registry.

malice_analysis.why_suspicious: The inclusion of large, non-software media files in a software package repository is highly abnormal and suggests abuse of the platform for unauthorized content distribution.
malice_analysis.violated_expectations: Normal npm packages contain JavaScript code or related assets for software development, not multi-gigabyte video files or unrelated media.
malice_analysis.similar_legitimate_use: Legitimate packages may include small media assets (e.g., icons, demo images) as part of a UI library, but not full-length movies or unrelated media.
key_indicators: Presence of large .ts video files in package root
JSON files with time-synced comments unrelated to software functionality
Package size (~54.5 MB) far exceeding typical npm package norms
No actual executable code or software functionality

attack_chain.action: Attacker creates and publishes npm packages with large video (.ts) and JSON files containing time-synced comments.
attack_chain.leads_to: Packages are available for download, enabling distribution of pirated movies and metadata via npm.

attack_chain.action: Users (or automated systems) download these packages, retrieving the media content from the npm registry.
attack_chain.leads_to: Circumvention of content controls, potential copyright infringement, and pollution of the software supply chain.

behavioral_signatures: npm packages containing large binary media files (.ts, .mp4, etc.)
Packages with no executable code or software functionality
Packages with JSON files containing time-synced comments or unrelated metadata
file_indicators: *.ts (MPEG transport stream video files) in package root
Package size > 50 MB with no code
network_indicators: Unusually large package downloads from npm registry
No external network activity from the package itself (since no code is executed)
detection_knowledge.how_to_detect: Flag npm packages that contain large binary media files (e.g., .ts, .mp4) and lack executable code. Monitor for packages with sizes significantly above the norm (e.g., >50 MB) and inspect for the presence of non-software assets such as video files or unrelated JSON metadata. Automated scanning can alert on packages with these characteristics for further review.
